entries.value: Barbarian invasion — Saxons, Picts, Irish, or some older terror
Colonial incursion from a greater power — Rome, or a former Roman province
Decadent society — internal collapse of values and will
Divine wrath upon them — plague, famine, drought sent as punishment
Domineering neighbour — tribute demanded, hostages taken, autonomy stripped
Economic collapse — trade routes cut, coinage debased, silver mines exhausted
Failed external war — a campaign that ruined the fighting men and emptied the granaries
Ideological divide — a religious schism, a dispute over custom, a heresy
Incompetent governance — a succession of bad rulers, a regency disaster
Internal refugees from disaster — famine, flood, or burning drove people from their homes
Loss of cultural confidence — a humiliation so great the people doubted their own worth
Magical calamity — a curse laid on the land, a faerie war, a sorcerer's blunder
Malevolent religion — a dark cult seized power, demanded tribute, corrupted the church
Miserable poverty — generations of hunger and bare survival
Natural disasters — floods, drought, bitter winters, plague of animals
Noble infighting — the lords tore themselves apart in blood feud and petty war
Religious or ideological excess — a purge, a crusade, a witch-hunt
Resource exhaustion — the forest, mine, or fishing grounds gave out
Scheming sorcerers — wizards manipulated or preyed upon the people
Some titanic monster — a dragon, a giant, a faerie lord turned enemy
Tyrannical rule — a warlord or corrupt king squeezed the people dry
Unsuccessful expansion — a war of conquest that went badly and cost everything
Usurpers seizing control — a coup, a betrayal, a false claimant
Vicious civil warfare — the people turned on each other
War with a stronger power — a devastating defeat from which recovery was slow
